author: Chaitanya Dadhwal
title: Jalen Brunson And Josh Hart Sound Off About Yaxel Lendeborg Saying He Lost Respect For Luka Doncic - NewsBreak
text:
By Chaitanya Dadhwal ,
1 hours ago
Luka Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers torched the Golden State Warriors 127-105 on the season-opening night after Yaxel Lendeborg trash-talked the Slovenian superstar . Doncic finished with 28 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, and three steals, shooting 7-18 from the field (38.9%) and 5-for-12 from three (41.7%).
Afterward, the 24-year-old rookie called out Luka Doncic for complaining and whining about fouls, saying he lost respect for the Lakers’ franchise player. This did not sit well with Doncic’s former teammate, Jalen Brunson , who had mixed reactions to Yaxel Lendeborg’s comments.
Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart recorded an episode of their podcast, ‘Roommates Show,’ where they both said it was acceptable for Lendeborg to trash-talk on the court, but he shouldn’t have made the postgame comments he did.
Here’s a transcript of their conversation on the podcast when Matt Hillman asked them if Yaxel Lendeborg was trash-talking too much as a rookie, in the context of his exchange with Luka Doncic.
Jalen Brunson: “Maybe to the media. I feel like people like to talk trash on court.”
Josh Hart: “Maybe dial down a little bit of the media, like, oh, I have no respect for him or something like that. You don’t really have to say that in the media. And I think he might have said it.”
Jalen Brunson: “When it comes to on the court, compete.”
Josh Hart: “Yeah, compete, do your thing. I think it’s good for the game. When you do that, there’s always a level of energy in the arena, so it’s cool.”
Jalen Brunson: “He’s playing great, though.”
Josh Hart: “Yeah, hooping.”
Jalen Brunson: “I think talking trash on the court is part of the game. We can say something to the media, whatever, but I feel like he just maybe said a little too much. You don’t have to say everything that’s on your mind, especially to the media.”
So it is safe to say that while they respect his game and trash-talk on the court, they don’t support him for speaking ill of Luka Doncic to the media. Here’s what Yaxel Lendeborg said to the media right after his first matchup on the court with the Slovenian superstar.
“I got to see what the NBA is like, man: a lot of flopping, a lot of flopping, a lot of praying to the ref, man… an interesting first game for me, for sure,” Lendeborg said, reflecting on his regular season debut with the Warriors.
“I had a lot of respect for him. But I didn’t watch the NBA much; I just watched the highlights. So I was seeing him kill people all the time. But being in there firsthand, watching all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect. Like, that was awful,” Yaxel Lendeborg added during his postgame press conference.
Brunson and Hart clearly believe trash talk is part of basketball and encourage Lendeborg to compete with confidence. However, they also believe there is a line between competition and disrespect.
For Jalen Brunson, that distinction likely carries extra weight given his close friendship and former partnership with Luka Doncic.
The Lakers and the Warriors have two more matchups left in the season, both in 2027 (January 21 and March 14). It remains to be seen whether Yaxel Lendeborg can perform well in those games to get his revenge.
